name: self-consistency
context: Reasoning tasks where a single sampled reasoning path may be unreliable. The agent samples multiple diverse reasoning chains for the same problem, then selects the most consistent answer via majority voting. Unlike chain-of-thought which is linear and single-pass, self-consistency is an ensemble method that improves accuracy at the cost of multiple LLM calls.
benefits: Significantly improves accuracy on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning
Simple to implement on top of existing CoT prompts
Works with any underlying reasoning prompt
tradeoffs: N× cost where N is the number of samples
Only works for tasks with a verifiable final answer
Diversity of samples depends on temperature and prompting
avoid_when: Open-ended generation tasks with no single correct answer
Tasks requiring creative or subjective outputs
anti_patterns: Using the same temperature for all samples (no diversity)
Voting on intermediate steps rather than final answers
Ignoring ties and defaulting to first sample
design_principles: Sample at least 5-10 times for meaningful majority
Use chain-of-thought prompting for each sample
Parse answers programmatically — do not rely on free-text comparison
best_practices: Normalize answer formats before voting (e.g., strip whitespace)
Log all sampled answers for post-hoc analysis
references: Wang et al., Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models, 2022 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171
